question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹1,200 at an interest rate of 3% per month in 7 months.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For Simple Interest, Total Interest % = Rate per period × Number of periods.

Total Interest % = 3% × 7 = 21%

Simple Interest = 21% of Principal

SI = (21 ÷ 100) × 1200 = 252

**∴ The correct answer is ₹252.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹1200

Rate of Interest (R) = 3% per month

Time (T) = 7 months

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 Simple Interest Calculation Timeline
 
• 
 
 
 0 Months
 
 ₹1200
 
 

 

 +3% (₹36)
 
 
 1 Month
 
 
• 
 
 

 

 

 Total 7 Months: 7 × ₹36 = ₹252
 
 
 7 Months
 
 SI = ₹252

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (1200 × 3 × 7) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 12 × 3 × 7

⇒ SI = 36 × 7

⇒ SI = 252

**∴ The correct answer is ₹252.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit of Time and Rate Match

In Simple Interest formulas, the unit of Time (T) must always match the unit of the Rate (R). Since the rate is given per month, the time should remain in months without converting to years.

Total Amount (A)

The final accumulated value including principal and interest is calculated using the formula A = P + SI.

Compound Interest vs Simple Interest

Unlike SI which is strictly calculated on the initial principal value over the period, Compound Interest is dynamically calculated on the accumulated amount. However, for the first period, SI and CI remain equal.
